claims.reason: Rests on NG202 1.1.1 (assess for OSAHS when two or more features are present, among them snoring, witnessed apnoeas and unexplained excessive sleepiness). The title pairs snoring with pauses in breathing or with sleepiness, so it meets that trigger. The source text is addressed to clinicians and does not itself tell the lay reader to report symptoms; the advice is derived.

scope_gaps.note: NG202 covers people over 16 and is an English NHS guideline; the sentence names NICE but states neither the age limit nor the setting. The assessment trigger is two or more features; the sentence does not mention the threshold.

NICE recommends fixed-level CPAP offered in addition to lifestyle advice, in people over 16; the sentence says none of this. The sentence does not claim that CPAP is the only option, and NICE lists alternatives (auto-CPAP, mandibular advancement splint).

A reader might assume that all cited sources are clinical guidelines on diagnosis and treatment. Only the two NICE NG202 chapters are; the third cited source is an NHS public-information page on insomnia.
NG202 sets the assessment trigger at two or more features; the sentence lists the three signs as alternatives.
The only matching source line is an insomnia self-care 'Don't' item, not advice about sleep apnoea; safe stopping and alternative travel are not in any snapshot.
The sentence prohibits self-selection of the device and settings; the source only describes clinician-led provision and follow-up.
The sentence attributes the choice to the treating clinician alone; NG202 describes shared decision-making and allows the person to decline CPAP.
